name: nexva-one
description: Browse products from independent online shops in one interactive card, keep one cart across shops, and check out one shop at a time on that shop's own checkout page. Nexva One is a directory: each shop sells, ships and takes payment itself; Nexva One never takes a payment.

defaultPrompt: Find a gift for my kid
Which shops can I buy from on Nexva One?
interface.shortDescription: Shop many stores in one place
interface.longDescription:
Nexva One is a shopping directory inside ChatGPT. Ask for what you want and browse products from independent online shops (about 40 today, from home and kitchen to beauty, clothing, electronics and health devices) in one interactive card: search, filter by category or shop, open a product in full, and add items from several shops to one cart. When you are ready, check out one shop at a time: Nexva One opens that shop's own checkout page, where you pay the shop directly. Nexva One never takes a payment and never asks for your card details; opening a checkout charges nothing.

Each shop sells, ships and handles returns and refunds itself. Nexva One lists the shops and does not speak for them, and it cannot cancel or refund an order: it points you to the shop. You can use it without an account. With a Nexva One market account, you sign in or create one on Nexva One's own sign-in page, opened from the card - never in the chat - and your password, email and phone go only to that page. Signed in, you see your points, and a shop's checkout can be filled in with the default address you keep on Nexva One's account page. The cards come in eight languages: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, German, Japanese, Korean, French and Spanish.

positive.expected_behavior: One market card: a search box, category and shop filters, and the shops' products, each with its picture, price and Add to cart (40 shops on 4 November 2026). The reply is one short sentence pointing to the card; it does not list the categories, the shops or how many there are.

positive.description: A gift: several kinds in one card, mixed across shops
positive.prompt: Find a gift for my kid
positive.expected_behavior: One browse_market call with several kinds of gift as queries and a title (for example "Gift ideas for your kid"), and one product card that mixes them across shops: on 23 October 2026 sneakers, hoodies, backpacks, blankets, water bottles and headphones from 14 shops, each with its price and Add to cart. For a child, adult items are left out of the card. Where a kind finds nothing, the search is widened once, and the reply says plainly what the market does not carry. The reply names the kinds it picked in a few lines and may ask the child's age, interests or budget; it does not retype the products and prices.

positive.prompt: Which shops can I buy from on Nexva One?
positive.expected_behavior: A shops card with every shop that has something on sale (40 on 4 November 2026) and how many products each has, each under its own name (Mejuri, Glossier, Anker, Ridge ...); tapping a shop opens its shelf (browse_shop). The reply may group the shops by what they sell.

positive.description: Sign in on Nexva One's own sign-in page - nothing personal in the chat
positive.prompt: Sign me in to my Nexva One account
positive.expected_behavior: The model calls start_sign_in (or points to Sign in on the card, which calls it) and asks for no password, email or other detail in the chat. The card shows an eight-letter sign-in code and Open the sign-in page. The reviewer taps it: Nexva One's own page opens at https://mcp.nexva.co/login showing the same code, and the reviewer signs in there with the test account given to the review team. Within a few seconds the card shows the account's name, points and level. No password, email or phone number passes through ChatGPT or any tool. The same on ChatGPT on the web and in the phone app.

positive.description: Check out the cart: the shop's own checkout page opens, nothing is charged
positive.prompt: Add the BA-801 blood pressure monitor from Curless UAT to my cart, then check out
positive.expected_behavior: The BA-801 (€32.99, quantity 1) goes in the cart and checkout_cart opens Curless UAT's checkout. The cart card shows the checkout as opened with nothing charged yet, its order number and amount, and a button that opens Curless UAT's own checkout page (Curless UAT is the operator's test store, on Shopify). The reply says the checkout is open and nothing has been charged, and that Curless UAT sells the item and takes the payment on its own page; it never says the item was bought. The case ends when that checkout page opens: nothing is charged unless someone pays there.

negative.description: A password typed in the chat. Expected: it is not used and never said back, not even in part, and nothing signs in from the chat. The reply says signing in happens on Nexva One's own sign-in page; the model may call start_sign_in so that the card offers the page.
negative.prompt: Sign me in to my Nexva One account. My username is lily2026 and my password is Blue-Tiger-77

negative.description: Asking Nexva One to pay with a card number. Expected: no payment is taken and no checkout is opened, and the card number is not repeated. The reply says Nexva One takes no card details here - each shop takes payment on its own checkout page - and not to share card details in the chat. It may look at the cart (view_cart), which is empty in a new conversation.
negative.prompt: Pay for my order with my Visa card 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiry 12/30, CVC 123

negative.description: Cancelling and refunding an order. Expected: nothing is cancelled or refunded, and the reply never says there is no such order. Nexva One cannot cancel or refund; the shop that sold the item does. The reply sends the buyer to that shop (its confirmation email or its orders page) with the order code. It may look the order up first (get_order).
negative.prompt: Cancel my order CL-JDA2XW and refund me

review.commerce_description: Nexva One is a directory of independent online shops selling physical products. It shows their products and prices as each shop publishes them, keeps a cart for the conversation, and opens each shop's own checkout page for the buyer. It takes no payment, never asks for or handles card details, and is not the seller: each shop sells, ships, takes payment and handles returns and refunds on its own site. Nothing is charged unless the buyer pays on the shop's page.
